mainEntity.name: What is a fractional Head of PR and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional Head of PR is a senior comms leader who joins your team part-time, owns strategy and execution, and operates with the same accountability as a full-time hire but without the salary, benefits and equity cost. It is the right fit for Web3, AI, DePIN and cybersecurity founders who need more than a PR agency can give: strategic ownership, narrative leadership, board-level comms, and someone who is genuinely embedded. See when to hire fractional PR for the stage-by-stage decision criteria.

mainEntity.name: How much does a fractional Head of PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional engagement runs $5K–$12K per month depending on scope, hours and the cadence of execution required. A focused launch sprint runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks. Both remove the multi-person account-team markup built into a traditional agency retainer of $15K–$45K per month, and the full salary overhead of a full-time head count at $180K–$250K per year. For a direct comparison of the models see fractional PR vs in-house hire 2026.

mainEntity.name: What outlets and deliverables can I expect?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deliverables depend on what you are launching, but a typical fractional engagement covers: narrative positioning, a 90-day coverage calendar, direct pitching to tier-1 crypto outlets (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, Blockworks), op-ed drafting and placement, KOL briefing and wave coordination, APAC localisation across Korea, Japan, China, India and SEA, and AI-citation tracking. Coverage is driven by real news hooks, not wire blasts or placement-guarantee contracts.

mainEntity.name: What does the process look like from first contact to live?

acceptedAnswer.text: A short project brief or 30-minute call is all that is needed to start. Within 48 hours you get a read on your current press footprint and a proposed scope. Onboarding takes one week: access to your team channels, a review of existing materials and a first narrative session. Week two is the coverage calendar and first pitches going out. Most founders see their first tier-1 placement within three to six weeks, depending on news readiness. The full four-step process is described in the "how it runs" section above.
